summary: This paper systematically completes and sharpens the fixed-angle equiangular line program in Section 5 of Djaljapayan, Liao, and Yu (arXiv:2611.34855v1). Theorem 1 proves an exact linear-in-a classification of nontrivial relative-bound seeds (k,M,a) with positive Bukh-Cox slope Lk > M/b: only k in {3,5,6,7} (a=3) and k in {a^2-3, a^2-2} (odd a >= 5) qualify, and k=a^2-3 yields an exact rational constant and slope. Theorem 2 establishes the tight alternating-character circulant range lambda_alt(A) in [-3,1] (sharpening Q-2r to Q-6), bounds r <= b-1, and constructs explicit {+-1}^M eigenvectors Sv = -3v for all four a=3 seeds enabling odd-t repetitions with constant Schur ratio rho = k/a. This unlocks four new infinite fixed-angle families (k=3,5,6,22), sharpens thresholds for k=7 (319->245) and k=23 (5599->5267), and reveals exact zero-gap adjacent +2 jumps. Theorem 3 upgrades DLY Theorem 5.2 to linearly growing consecutive intervals and generalizes DLY Proposition 5.3 to infinite s in {2,3} block windows for odd q >= 5, with sharp Pell-equation jumps and an s >= 4 barrier. Eighteen core algebraic theorems are verified in constructive Lean 4.35.0 alongside 16 zero-float SHA-256 certificates and 56 tests.
strengths: Complete, exact algebraic classification of all positive-slope relative-bound seeds (Theorem 1), uncovering the rational Bukh-Cox branch k = a^2 - 3.

Sharp spectral improvements (lambda_alt in [-3,1], r <= b - 1) and explicit {+-1}^M eigenvectors for all four a = 3 seeds, yielding four new infinite families, strictly improved odd-q thresholds for k = 7 and k = 23, and exact adjacent-dimension +2 jumps.
Clean consecutive-dimension generalizations of DLY Theorem 5.2 and Proposition 5.3, including Pell-equation boundary sharpness and an exact s >= 4 impossibility barrier.

Exemplary machine verification: 18 constructive Lean 4.35.0 theorems (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 custom axioms) paired with an AST-audited zero-float rational/Q(sqrt(p)) verifier, 16 SHA-256 certificates, and 56 adversarial tests.
weaknesses: While Theorem 1 classifies parameter triples for all odd a >= 5, actual realizations of relative-bound seeds at k in {a^2-3, a^2-2} are only known for a in {3, 5}, leaving a >= 7 conditional on open seed existence.

Odd-t seed-eigenvector extensions are not obtained for the a = 5 seeds (Higman-Sims k = 22 and Leech k = 23), so whether {+-1}^M eigenvectors with Sv = -5v exist to further lower q0(22) and q0(23) remains open.

The Lean 4 formalization covers the core algebraic identities and inequalities over Nat/Int, while matrix rank, PSDness, and circulant/Golay constructions are checked separately in the exact Python/Q(sqrt(p)) suite.
